reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
setup: Basel III standardized approach for operational risk. Marginal coefficients on the Business Indicator (BI): 12% on the first EUR 1bn, 15% on the slice from EUR 1bn to EUR 30bn, 18% on everything above EUR 30bn. The bank's BI is EUR 40bn and the internal loss multiplier is set to 1.
ask: Operational risk capital is closest to:

options.label: ≈ EUR 630m
options.why: Decimal slip: the right figure is EUR 6.27bn, and 0.627 was read as EUR 627m (ten times too small).

options.label: ≈ EUR 1,800m
options.why: Charged only the top slice, 18% × EUR 10bn, and dropped the two lower slices (120 and 4,350).

options.label: ≈ EUR 40,000m
options.why: Took the BI itself as the charge and never applied the marginal coefficients.

takeaway: Marginal coefficients apply slice by slice: the 15% middle slice does most of the work even for a very large bank.

reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
setup: Standardized approach, internal loss multiplier $ILM = \ln[e - 1 + (LC/BIC)^{0.8}]$, where $LC = 15 \times$ average annual loss. Ten years of verified losses (EUR bn): 3.8, 2.9, 2.8, 2.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.1, 0.2, 0.1, 0.2. The Business Indicator Component is $BIC$ = EUR 18bn.
ask: Is the ILM above 1, below 1, or exactly 1?

options.label: Below 1
options.why: Used the average loss of 1.39 as $LC$ and left out the factor of 15. Then $LC/BIC = 0.077$ and ILM $\approx 0.61$.

options.label: Exactly 1
options.why: ILM equals 1 only when $LC = BIC$ (the bracket is then $e$). Here $LC = 20.85$ against $BIC = 18$.

takeaway: ILM crosses 1 exactly where $LC = BIC$: a loss component above the BIC pushes capital above the BIC.

reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
setup: Default Basel rules, no national discretion. A bank has a Business Indicator of EUR 960m and ten years of annual losses averaging EUR 352m (peak EUR 0.9bn). Coefficients: 12% up to EUR 1bn. In the lowest BI bucket the internal loss multiplier is not driven by the loss history. The loss component is $15 \times$ average loss.
ask: Operational risk capital is closest to:

options.label: ≈ EUR 12m
options.why: Coefficient slip: applied 1.2% instead of 12%, ten times too small.

options.label: ≈ EUR 360m
options.why: Pushed the heavy loss history through the ILM formula. In bucket 1 the ILM is fixed at 1, so losses do not enter.

options.label: ≈ EUR 5,300m
options.why: Reported the loss component ($15 \times 352$) as if it were the capital requirement.

takeaway: Below EUR 1bn of BI, capital is just 12% of BI. Loss history only matters from bucket 2 up.

reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
setup: A bank has a Business Indicator of EUR 34.5bn. The marginal coefficients are 12% on the first EUR 1bn, 15% on the slice from EUR 1bn to EUR 30bn and 18% on the part above EUR 30bn. The Business Indicator Component is the sum of the three slices.
ask: Which of the three slices contributes most to the BIC?

options.label: The 12% slice (first EUR 1bn)
options.why: It has the smallest rate and the narrowest band: $12\% \times 1 = 0.12$bn.

options.label: The 18% slice (above EUR 30bn)
options.why: The 18% rate is the highest, but it only applies to EUR 4.5bn of BI: $18\% \times 4.5 = 0.81$bn.

takeaway: A slice's contribution is rate times width. The middle slice is 29 times wider than the first, so it dominates.

reading: ORR-24: Basel III: Finalising Post-Crisis Reforms
setup: Standardized approach. Marginal coefficients: 12% on the first EUR 1bn of BI, 15% on the slice from EUR 1bn to EUR 30bn, 18% above. A bank has a Business Indicator of EUR 13bn, so $12\% \times 13 = 1.56$ and $15\% \times 13 = 1.95$ (EUR bn).

options.label: Above 15% of BI (above EUR 1.95bn)
options.why: No slice is charged above 15%, and part of BI is charged at only 12%, so the blended rate cannot exceed 15%.

options.label: Between 12% and 15% of BI, just under the 15% end
Below 12% of BI (under EUR 1.56bn)
options.why: The lowest coefficient is 12% and it applies to just EUR 1bn. The other EUR 12bn is charged at 15%, so the blended rate is well above 12%.

takeaway: The blended rate is a weighted average of the marginal rates. It sits between them and moves toward the top rate as BI grows.
